text: Asthma review. Poorly controlled despite current therapy. Current meds: fluticasone 250 mcg inhaler twice daily, salbutamol 100 mcg as needed. Patient quit smoking in 2019; mother still smokes at home. Referral to respirology sent.
Respirology consultation. Spirometry shows reversible airflow obstruction. Impression: severe eosinophilic asthma. Plan: trial of omalizumab.
Respirology follow-up. Omalizumab started 2024-05-15 and stopped 2024-09-10 due to lack of response. Continue inhaled therapy.
Asthma exacerbation with wheeze and cough. Prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days.
Emergency visit for asthma exacerbation. Nebulized salbutamol given. Discharged on prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days.
Respirology review. Diagnosis of severe eosinophilic asthma reconfirmed today. Remains symptomatic on high-dose inhaled corticosteroid with good technique and adherence.
Gout flare, left first MTP joint. Prednisone 30 mg daily for 5 days. Asthma stable.
Asthma exacerbation after a viral upper respiratory infection. Prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days. Switched from fluticasone 250 mcg to fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 mcg one inhalation twice daily.
Complete blood count. Collected 2026-06-28. Eosinophils 0.45 x10^9/L.
Reprinted report. Complete blood count. Collected 2025-11-10. Eosinophils 0.62 x10^9/L.
Patient asks about Drug Z. Re-referred to respirology to discuss biologic options. Old referral form on file lists PHN SYNTH-PHN-0009, which is incorrect.
Active medications: fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 mcg one inhalation twice daily; salbutamol 100 mcg as needed; montelukast 10 mg daily.
